structure Local (X : Listing G n) (p : BudgetPoint) (v : Source G n) (H w : ℝ) : Prop where
  smooth i : p.Regular (X.reg i).support (v.logRead i)
  family : (X.read v).ForcedFamily p
  transforms s b : Nonempty ((X.read v).Moves s b)
  cheap : ∃ u, (∀ i, p.supBounds (X.reg i).site (X.reg i).support (v.logRead i) (u i)) ∧ Quotes.early p X.reg u H
  expensive : ∃ k, (∀ i, 0 ≤ k i ∧ ∀ U, ‖v.hardRead i U‖ ≤ k i) ∧ Ac.Hit (fun i => (X.hard i).support) p.B k (p.supportExponent+1) w

evidence: [M] prints that fixed local families f_{i,u}, k_{i,u} and a continuous scalar tau_u satisfy (13.10)-(13.12), and its proof says 'Flat evaluation gives continuity of the scalar'. Offering.holds concludes only `∃ X v, ∃ (τ : ℝ → ℝ) ..., (∀ x∈s, atlas ... (v x) (τ x)) ∧ (∀ x∈s, Local ...) ∧ Compared X (B.a.budget m) v s`; neither atlas, Local nor Compared (whose fields `values`/`series` concern only X.read (a x)) mentions continuity of τ, and glazing just supplies τ := stanzaFee Z d M with no ContinuousOn lemma for it anywhere in [L]. The only continuity downstream is Curve.v for the output vacuum vac (V' x) (τ x) = τ x - flat value, obtained in Mallow.Spring.moves via machine.run, which is a statement about the next-stage representative, not about τ, and recovering continuity of τ from it needs an unwritten argument; so the claim stands as weaker, and [M]'s deliberate proof sentence shows it is not a typo.

[M] prints that fixed local families f_{i,u}, k_{i,u} "and a continuous scalar tau_u" satisfy (13.10)-(13.12), with equivariance, weighted continuity, regularity and restriction. Use.Offering (proved by Rain.glazing with tau := stanzaFee Z d M) gives only "exists (τ : ℝ → ℝ) ... (∀ x∈s, atlas ... (Q x) X (v x) (τ x)) ∧ (∀ x∈s, Local ...) ∧ Compared X (B.a.budget m) v s"; atlas is a pointwise identity, and Compared constrains only the families X.read (v x), never τ. Continuity of τ is not stated in Offering, glazing, or anywhere for stanzaFee; Return.reset only yields ContinuousOn of the output vacuum (F x).v = vac (v x) (τ x) via Curve, which gives τ's continuity only by an unwritten argument (continuity of the log-read sum plus flat evaluation). So the claim stands as weaker; [M]'s proof explicitly argues "Flat evaluation gives continuity of the scalar", so this is not a typo.
